newsitem.title: ITALY: Banca di Roma strikes over lay-off plans.
newsitem.headline: Banca di Roma strikes over lay-off plans.

text.p: Staff at Italy's Banca di Roma group went on strike on Tuesday against planned lay-offs as the government prepared for talks with union leaders and the banking association ABI to try to solve the problem across the sector.

Several hundred workers at Banca di Roma and the Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura and Banca Mediterranea, which also belong to the group, joined the strike in protest at more than 4,000 layoffs planned in a group restructuring programme.
A statement from banking unions involved in the strike said some 6,000 people also took part in a demonstration in Rome.
ABI chairman Maurizio Sella told reporters that he expected the government to call talks on Wednesday to examine the problem of lay-offs throughout the banking sector.
"We presume the government will call us in tomorrow," he said. "We and the unions will be in two separate rooms and the government will mediate between the different positions."
An ABI delegation earlier met Cabinet Undersecretary Enrico Micheli, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu and Treausry Undersecretary Roberto Pinza.
Asked whether an agreement could be reached, Sella said: "We're still working on it. We'll see if we manage to reach one by tomorrow."
Analysts say the Italian banking sector is hugely overstaffed and radical restructuring is needed if it is to achieve the sort of profitability seen elsewhere in Europe.
